channel.title: doyouknow.app - English
channel.description: Surprising facts about UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the world.

item.title: How Cultural Gift-Giving Etiquette Differs Worldwide
item.description: From China's red envelopes to Japan's wrapping rituals, the customs, taboos, and etiquette that shape how gifts are given and received around the world.

item.title: How Dubai's Desalination Plants Actually Work
item.description: Almost all of Dubai's drinking water comes from the sea. Here is how the desalination technology, energy tradeoffs, and storage systems behind that actually work.

item.title: How Facial Recognition Bias Happens
item.description: How facial recognition systems end up performing unevenly across skin tone, gender, and age, and what NIST testing and researchers have found about the causes.

item.title: How Flash Sales Manipulate Buying Decisions
item.description: Why limited-time flash sales trigger impulsive purchases, and what psychology and retail research reveal about the tactics behind the countdown clock.

item.title: How Hajj Logistics Are Actually Managed Each Year
item.description: How Saudi Arabia manages the annual Hajj: quotas, the Nusuk platform, transit, crowd engineering after Mina, heat risk, and medical response.

item.title: How Museum Lighting Is Designed to Protect Art
item.description: Why museum galleries are kept dim, how conservators measure light in lux-hours, and the science behind protecting paintings, textiles, and paper from fading.

item.title: How Noise-Cancelling Headphones Actually Work
item.description: How active noise cancellation uses microphones and inverted sound waves to cancel noise, why it works better on engine drone than voices, and its real limits.

item.title: How the Forgetting Curve Shapes Study Habits
item.description: Hermann Ebbinghaus mapped how fast memory fades over a century ago, and his forgetting curve still shapes how researchers design effective study habits today.

item.title: How the Placebo Effect Actually Works
item.description: The real neuroscience behind placebos: brain chemistry, conditioning, pill color, sham surgery, and why belief can measurably change the body.

item.title: How Vaccination Herd Immunity Actually Works
item.description: The real math behind herd immunity: reproduction numbers, vaccination thresholds, waning protection, and why the concept is more fragile than it sounds.

item.title: How Video Game Remasters Are Actually Made
item.description: How remasters differ from remakes and ports, and the technical, legal, and business realities behind bringing classic games back.

item.title: Why AI Chatbots Sometimes Hallucinate Facts
item.description: Why large language models confidently generate false information, how next-word prediction makes this unavoidable, and what researchers are doing to reduce it.

item.title: Why Cold Plunge Culture Keeps Growing
item.description: Why cold plunging spread from elite athlete recovery to a mainstream daily ritual, and what the physiology research actually supports.

item.title: Why the Dubai Frame Became an Instant Landmark
item.description: How Zabeel Park's giant picture-frame structure turned a design-credit dispute and a glass sky bridge into one of Dubai's fastest-known landmarks.

item.title: Why Eye Contact Norms Vary by Culture
item.description: Why direct eye contact signals confidence in some cultures and disrespect in others, and what psychology and anthropology reveal about it.

item.title: Why Handwriting Practice Still Matters in a Digital Age
item.description: Why researchers keep finding real learning benefits from handwriting even as keyboards and AI tools take over most everyday writing.

item.title: Why Multigenerational Households Are Rising Again
item.description: Housing costs, aging parents, and cultural shifts are pushing more American families back into homes with three or more generations under one roof.

item.title: Why Some People Never Get Hangovers
item.description: The real science of hangovers: acetaldehyde, genetics, congeners, dehydration, and why a lucky few seem to escape the morning after unscathed.

item.title: Why We Forget Dreams So Quickly
item.description: The neuroscience of why vivid dreams vanish within minutes of waking, from brain chemistry during REM sleep to why some people recall dreams and others rarely do.

item.title: Why Your Phone Battery Degrades Over Time
item.description: Why lithium-ion phone batteries lose capacity with age, what actually happens inside the cell during charge cycles, and which habits genuinely slow the decline.
